 Judgment

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in at road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 04-06-2020 at about 5.20 a.m., near 150th Mile, on Madanapalli-Punganur road,
NH-42 H/O Valasapalli Village, Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh, when the petitioner was riding a two-wheeler bearing No.AP-03-M-4106, slowly and steadily, following all traffic rules and regulations, along with his younger brother, at that time the driver of the passenger auto-rickshaw bearing No.AP-03-X-6765 came in rash and negligently,
without caring for human safety and dashed to the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Government Hospital and then Helious Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, he was working as mechanic and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Madanapalli Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said auto for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.1 appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.2 did not choose to appear and remained absent.
Hence, the respondent No.2 is placed ex-parte.
4. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.2, in respect of T.Kishore vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12041343/
2

sentences.text: Auto-rickshaw bearing No. AP-03-X-6765 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(C) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.

It has further contended that, the driver of the offending autorickshaw was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident and the vehicle was not having valid permit and fitness certificate.
Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of the respondent No.2, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

It has contended that,
as per the police documents, the petitioner was solely responsible for the accident.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
Further it is contended that, the respondent No.2 knowing that his driver was not having valid and effective driving licence to drive the auto-rickshaw, has entrusted the said vehicle to him.
Further, the said auto-rickshaw was not having valid permit and fitness certificate as on the date of accident.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 04- 06-2020 at about 5:20 a.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Passenger Auto,
bearing registration No. AP-03-X-6765 ?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
6. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 13 documents as Ex.P.1 to 13.
Further, he has got examined one more witness namely Dr. Chidanand as P.W.2 and closed his side.

On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has examined its Administrative Officer as R.W.1 and got marked 5 documents as Ex.R.1 to 5 and closed its side.
7.
I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

8. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 9. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 04-06-2020 at about 5.20 a.m., near 150th Mile, on Madanapalli-Punganur road, NH-42 H/O Valasapalli Village, Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh,

Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident, he was working as mechanic and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
10. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 13 documents as Ex.P.1 to 13.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of accident information report, Ex.P.4 is true copy of sketch, Ex.P.5 is true copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.6 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.7 is discharge summary,
Ex.P.8 are medical bills (total 43), Ex.P.9 are prescriptions (total 25), Ex.P.10 are lab reports (total 3), Ex.P.11 are hospital records (total 7), Ex.P.12 is clinical record and Ex.P.13 are x-rays (total 2).

11. At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, the date, time and place of accident, the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident, the issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.1, in respect of passenger auto-rickshaw bearing No. AP-03-X-6765 and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

Further, the above oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/respondent No.2, as it did not choose to appear and contest the case of petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.1 insurance company though has specifically denied the said facts in its written statement, it has not produced any rebuttal evidence to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

The petitioner/P.W.1 has unequivocally denied the suggestion made by the learned counsel for respondent No.1 in his cross-examination that, the said accident has occurred due to his own rash and negligent riding of motorcycle and there is not fault on the part of driver of auto-rickshaw bearing No. AP-03-X-6765.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.

On the other hand, except the self serving statements of R.W.1, who is the representative of respondent No.1 insurance company, there is absolutely no other oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondent No.1 to show that, the petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident taken place due to his own rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle bearing No.AP-03-M-4106 and there is no fault or negligence on the part of the driver of offending auto- rickshaw bearing No. AP-03-X-6765.
12.

On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 6, prima-facia it reveals that, on 04-06- 2020 at about 5.20 a.m., near 150th Mile, on Madanapalli- Punganur road,
NH-42 H/O Valasapalli Village, Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh, when the petitioner was riding a two- wheeler bearing No.AP-03-M-4106, slowly and cautiously, the offending auto-rickshaw bearing Reg.
No.AP-03-X-6765, being driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner, came from opposite T.Kishore vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12041343/
4 direction and dashed to the motorcycle of the petitioner.

sentences.text: Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

The investigation officer in his Ex.P.5 final report/charge-sheet, has clearly stated that, the said accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No. AP-03-X-6765.
13.

The Ex.P.3 spot mahazer also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on extreme left side of Madanapalle-Punganur road, National Highway-42, near 150th mile, Valasapalli village,
Madanapalle Mandal.
Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh, in between motorcycle bearing No.AP-03-M-4106 and on coming offending auto-rickshaw bearing No.AP-03-X-6765.
Further, it is not the case of respondent No.1 that, the accident is caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle bearing No.AP-03-X-6765 and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner/rider of motorcycle bearing No.AP-03-M-4106, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending auto-rickshaw.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondent No.1 and even nothing is elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the petitioner or else there was any contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner in the cause of accident.

The investigation officer in his Ex.P.5 final report/charge-sheet, has clearly stated that, the said accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending auto-rickshaw bearing Reg.
No.AP- 03-X-6765.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the owner or the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.AP-03-X-6765.

In such circumstances,
there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident 14.

Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.6 wound certificate, Ex.P.7 discharge summary,
Ex.P.10 lab reports, Ex.P.11 hospital records, Ex.P.12 clinical record and Ex.P.13 x-rays, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and he has suffered bicolumnar acetabulum fracture right, compound subtrochanteric fracture right, right fracture distal end radius and right inferior pubic rami fracture.
The same is deposed by P.W.2, who is the doctor who has clinically examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondent No.1, to show that the above medical records are false documents.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondent No.1 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No.AP-03-X-6765 and the injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
15. It is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) SCC T.Kishore vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12041343/
5 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

sentences.text: 16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
17. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 04-06-2020 at about 5:20 p.m., near 150th Mile on Madanapalli-Punganur road, NH-42, Valasapalli Village, Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of auto- rickshaw bearing Reg. No.
AP-03-X-6765.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident in question is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending auto- rickshaw bearing Reg. No. AP-03-X-6765 and he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner,
he has suffered bicolumnar acetabulum fracture right, compound subtrochanteric fracture right,
right fracture distal end radius and right inferior pubic rami fracture and for the said injuries he has undergone surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has not produced any relevant document.
In the petition, the age of petitioner as on the date of accident is mentioned as 38 years.
Likewise, in all the medical records, produced and got marked by the petitioner as Ex.P.7, 10 and 11, his age is mentioned as 38 years.
On the other hand, in the instant case, the age of the petitioner, as on the date of accident, is not specifically denied or seriously disputed by the respondent No.1.
Even, there is no contrary material on record, which creates doubt on the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
There is absolutely no reason to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Therefore, in such circumstances, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident is considered as 38 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of T.Kishore vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12041343/
6 assessment of his disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered bicolumnar acetabulum fracture right,
compound subtrochanteric fracture right, right fracture distal end radius and right inferior pubic rami fracture.

sentences.text: Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, there is 22.5% physical disability to the whole body of the petitioner.
The oral evidence of P.W.2 is fully corroborated with documentary evidence.

The above medical records placed on record by the petitioner clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and he has suffered bicolumnar acetabulum fracture right, compound subtrochanteric fracture right, right fracture distal end radius and right inferior pubic rami fracture.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, there is no disability to the petitioner and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.
Further he has denied that, there are no restrictions of movements to the petitioner.

But, it is pertinent to note that,
the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 04-06-2020 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 24-08-2023, which is after lapse of three years and two months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further he has stated that, the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

entities.text: Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
If the disability had been assessed after future surgery,
perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.
Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his cross-examination that, the fractures are united.

Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 15% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 15% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as mechanic and was earning income of Rs.25,000/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do mechanic work.
The respondent No.1 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before the accident he was doing mechanic work and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.

Therefore, in such circumstances,
there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2020.

Hence,
the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.14,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,74,000/-.
b)

As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 38 years is 15.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,74,000 X 15/100 X 15 = Rs.3,91,500/-.

7 ii) Medical expenses:

entities.text: T.Kishore vs United India Ins Co Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.5,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 43 medical bills, as per Ex.P.8.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that, the bills at serial No.40 to 42 are advance receipts.
Therefore, the said bills are not taken into consideration.

Accordingly, it is held that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.4,25,127/-
towards medical expenses and he is entitled for the said amount under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:

In the present case, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e.
suffered bicolumnar acetabulum fracture right, compound subtrochanteric fracture right, right fracture distal end radius and right inferior pubic rami fracture.

As per Ex.P.7 discharge summary,
the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 06 days from 04-01-2021 to 09-01-2021, in Helios Hospital, Tirupathi.
Further, as per P.W.2, the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner,
this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.40,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:
As per Ex.P.7 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 06 days from 04-01-2021 to 09-01-2021, in Helios Hospital, Tirupathi.
He might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period.

Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 6 = Rs.6,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:
As per Ex.P.7 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 06 days from 04-01-2021 to 09-01-2021, in Helios Hospital, Tirupathi.
He might have spent considerable amount towards food and nourishment during that period.

Therefore,
compensation of Rs.800 x 6 = Rs.4,800/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Buggakduva, Madanapalli, Chittoor,
Andhra Pradesh, the accident has taken place near 150th Mile on Madanapalli-Punganur road,
NH-42 H/o Valasapalli Village, Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh and the petitioner has taken treatment at Helios Hospital, Tirupathi.
Taking into consideration the distance in between both the places

,
compensation of Rs.4,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has taken treatment for 6 days as inpatient at Helios Hospital, Tirupathi, for the grievous injuries sustained by him.
He might have taken rest for about 2 months and lost his income for the said period.

Therefore, Rs.14,500 x 2 =
Rs.29,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 38 years and unfortunately he has suffered bicolumnar acetabulum fracture right, compound subtrochanteric fracture right, right fracture distal end radius and right inferior pubic rami fracture.
The evidence shows that, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 15% to the whole body.

Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/-
T.Kishore vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12041343/
8 towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.

entities.text: T.Kishore vs United India Ins Co Ltd

sentences.text: ix) Future medical expenses:
The P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants for which approximate cost of Rs.30,000/- is required.
But, admittedly, he has not issued estimation of cost for the said surgery or for further treatment.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.

19. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows:
1. Loss of future income Rs. 3,91,500-00 2.
Medical expenses 4,25,127-00 3. Pain and sufferings 40,000-00 4.
Attendant charges 6,000-00 5.
Food and nourishment 4,800-00 6.
Conveyance expenses 4,000-00 7. Loss of income during 29,000-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 20,000-00
9. Future medical expenses 20,000-00

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.9,40,427/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
20. Liability:
Now the question before this Court is, who is liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.

Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the insurer,
respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending passenger auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No.
AP-03-X-6765.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the accident is question has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.AP-03-X-6765 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.

The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the vehicle is required to indemnify the respondent No.1.
21.

But, the respondent No.1 has taken specific defence in the case that, as on the date of accident the driver of offending vehicle was not holding valid driving licence to drive the said vehicle and the respondent No.2 knowing that his driver was not having valid and effective driving licence to drive T.Kishore vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12041343/
9 the said auto-rickshaw, has entrusted the said vehicle to him.

entities.text: T.Kishore vs United India Ins Co Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further he has contended that, the said auto-rickshaw was not having valid permit and fitness certificate as on the date of accident.
Hence, the respondent No.1 insurance company is not liable to indemnify the insured/owner of offending vehicle i.e. respondent No.2.

In such circumstances, the burden was on the respondent No.2 to establish that, as on the date of accident the driver of offending vehicle was holding valid &
effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle and it was having valid permit and fitness certificate to ply the said vehicle at the place of accident.
22. The respondent No.2 has failed to discharge the said burden.

He has not produced any document to establish that, as on the date of accident the driver of offending vehicle was holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the offending passenger auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No.
AP-03-X-6765 and the said vehicle was having valid permit and fitness certificate to ply the said vehicle at the place of accident.

On the other hand, the documents produced and got marked by the respondent No.1 in the evidence of R.W.1, as Ex.R.1 to 5, clearly goes to show that, as on the date of accident, the offending auto-rickshaw bearing No.AP-03-X-6765 was insured at the respondent No.1 insurance company and the policy was valid as on the date of accident.

Further, it reveals that, as on the date of accident the driver of offending vehicle by name Balaji Naik S/o Narayana Naik was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the offending auto-rickshaw.
As per Ex.R.3 driving licence, the said driver was holding licence to drive Light Motor Vehicle Non-Transport (ARNT) and Motorcycle With Gear (MCWG) vehicle only.
He was not permitted to drive Light Motor Vehicle Transport (ART).
Further, the Ex.R.4 Permit History Report clearly speaks that, the permit with respect to auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No. AP-03-X-6765 was expired on 11-05-2014 and since then it is not been renewed.

23. The learned counsel for respondent No.1 vehemently argued that, the Ex.R.2 Insurance Policy clearly speaks that, the policy covers the risk provided the driver of insured vehicle holds an effective driving licence at the time of accident and he is not disqualified from holding or obtaining such a licence.

Further, the Ex.R.3 driving licence of the driver of offending vehicle by name Balaji Naik S/o Narayana Naik and Ex.P.4 Permit History Report of vehicle bearing Reg. No. AP-03-X-6765 clearly speaks that, as on the date of accident the said driver was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the passenger auto- rickshaw or Light Motor Transport vehicle.

In such circumstances, the respondent No.2/owner of offending vehicle who consciously handed over his vehicle to a person who did not possess driving licence, cannot be permitted to take the benefit of his wrong and the respondent No.1/Insurance Company is entitled to raise a defence under Sec.149(2)
of Motor Vehicles Act.
24.

On the other hand, the learned counsel for petitioner vehemently argued that, it is settled principle of law that, the insurance company is liable to pay the third party and recover from the insured even if there is breach of any condition recognised under Sec.149(2) of M.V.Act, even if it is fundamental breach.

25. The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, in the case of New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Bijapur by its Divisional Manager V/s Yallavva and another, reported in ILR 2020 Kar 2239, has clearly held that,
" i) Having regard to Section 149(1) R/w Section 149(7), whenever a case falls under Section T.Kishore vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12041343/
10 149(2)(a) and the same is successfully established or proved by the Insurance Company, as per the twin tests laid by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Swaran Singh, nevertheless, the insurer or Insurance Company is liable to satisfy the award vis--vis a third party and is entitled to recover from the insured.

sentences.text: This is irrespective of, the policy being an Act policy in terms of Section 147 pertaining to compulsory coverage of risks of third parties and other classes of persons stated therein or a policy covering other risks by specific contract being entered into in that regard and where additional premium is paid by the insured i.e., a contractual policy.

ii) The Insurer is liable to pay the third party and recover from the insured even if there is breach of any condition recognized under Section 149 (2), even if it is a fundamental breach (that is breach of condition which is the cause for the accident) and the insurer proves the said breach in view of the mandate under Section 149(1) of the Act.

But, no such order can be passed against the insurer, if, on the facts and circumstances of a case, a finding is given by the court that the third party (injured or deceased) had played any fraud or was in collusion with the insured, individually or collectively, for a wrongful gain to themselves or cause wrongful loss to the insurer.

iii) The Court can also fasten the absolute liability on the insurer, if there is any breach of condition which is enumerated under Section 149(2) of the Act or any other condition of the policy if the Insurance Company has waived breach of any such condition or has taken the special responsibility to pay by collecting extra premium by covering any type of risk depending upon facts of each case.
iv) Thus, the rule of pay and recover is applicable in view of the mandate in Section 149(4) of the Act and even if there is a breach of the terms of the insurance policy, the insurer is bound to satisfy the judgment and award as if it were a judgment debtor, even if it satisfies the twin tests enunciated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court under Section 149(4)(a) of the Act.
v) Before passing any order on the Insurance Company to pay and recover, the Court has to examine the facts and circumstances of each case and if it finds that the victim, injured or the deceased, in a particular case, was solely or jointly responsible for breach of such fundamental condition by playing fraud or in collusion with the insured, the Court may exercise its discretion not to fasten the liability on the insurer.
vi) However, the court should not adopt the above guideline as a general rule in all cases, but only under peculiar facts and circumstances of each case and on giving appropriate reasons.
vii) If the Insurance Company makes out a case under Section 149(2)(b) of the Act, then also the Insurance Company has to satisfy the award so far as third party is concerned, as it is the duty of the Insurance Company to indemnify the insured on the basis of the policy of the insurance and even when the contract of insurance itself is void, nevertheless the liability to indemnify the insured would arise and insurer is entitled to recover from the insured.
viii) Thus, in a case where Section 149(2)(b) applies and the Insurance Company successfully establishes that the policy is void, in such a case also, the insurer is not absolved of its liability to satisfy the judgment or award as rights or obligations would flow even from a policy which is void T.Kishore vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12041343/
11 vis--vis third party.

sentences.text: In such a case, the insurer is not completely absolved of its liability, the insured would have to satisfy the award vis--vis the third party and recover from the insured the amount paid to the third party and may also have a right to seek damages from the insured.

ix) The judgment of the Division Bench of this Court in Subramanyam, holding that a pay and recovery order cannot be made as there is no liability to pay or satisfy the award or decree in respect of a case falling under Section 149(2) is not correct.

Hence, that portion of the judgment in Subramanyam, which states that if the case falls within the scope of Section 149(2) of the Act and the insurer is successful in establishing any of the defence as stated therein, it would be completely absolved of its liability to satisfy the award is also not correct and to that extent, it is held to be bad in law."

26. The documents placed on record by the respondent No.1 insurance company clearly establishes that, as on the date of alleged accident the driver of the offending auto- rickshaw bearing Reg.
No.AP-03-X-6765 was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle.
Further, the said vehicle was not having valid permit and fitness certificate to ply the said vehicle at the place of accident.

But, in the present facts and circumstances of the case, the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for respondent No.1 does not hold good, as there is no evidence on record to show that, the respondent No.2/owner of offending vehicle was having knowledge or he had consciously handed over his vehicle to a person who did not possess valid driving licence.
On the other hand, the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for petitioner holds good and the ratio laid down in the above cited decision is aptly applicable to case in hand.

The oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the respondent No.1 insurance company clearly establishes that, there is fundamental breach of insurance policy conditions by the owner of offending vehicle i.e. respondent No.2.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons and in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decision, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the respondent No.1 being the insurer of the offending vehicle is primarily liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner and later recover the same from the owner of offending vehicle/respondent No.2.

Accordingly, holding that the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.9,40,427/- from the respondent No.1, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
27. Issue No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.9,40,427/- (Rupees nine lakh forty thousand four hundred and twenty-seven only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realisation.

The respondent No.1 is directed to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner within two months from the date of this order and recover the same from the respondent No.2 in the very proceedings by filing an execution petition.
